title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets out rules to make sure that AI systems developed in the United States are safe, reliable, and trustworthy. The law requires researchers and companies to follow strict testing, transparency, and reporting practices, and it creates an oversight body to enforce these standards.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act aims to safeguard consumers against misleading AI practices. It establishes regulations for transparency and accountability in AI systems to prevent deceptive marketing and usage.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a legislative proposal aimed at strengthening the security and preparedness of advanced artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to establish standards, frameworks, and guidelines to protect against potential threats and ensure safe deployment of AI technologies.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a law designed to protect the integrity of elections by preventing and mitigating the use of AI-generated misinformation in campaign materials. It establishes rules for detecting deceptive AI content, requires transparency from political actors, and imposes penalties on those who spread or use false AI-generated messages to influence voters.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a new task force under the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to improve the security and resilience of artificial intelligence systems in the U.S. The act outlines the task force’s mission, structure, and coordination with other federal agencies, industry stakeholders, and academia to develop standards, share best practices, and respond to AI‑related cyber threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a federal law that establishes a comprehensive framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with the deployment and use of artificial intelligence systems. It creates oversight mechanisms, sets standards for AI safety and security, and mandates reporting and compliance requirements for organizations that develop or deploy AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 sets rules to guide the development, testing, and use of AI‑powered machines so they remain safe and transparent for the public. It creates a national framework where companies, regulators, and experts collaborate, share data, and monitor AI physical systems to reduce risks and promote responsible innovation.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This policy proposes an amendment to the Federal Election Campaign Act that would require any political ad containing AI‑generated images or video to include a clear statement that the content was created with artificial intelligence. The aim is to increase transparency and accountability in political advertising, and it may extend to other uses of AI‑generated content in political contexts.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act seeks to safeguard the integrity of elections by curbing the use of AI that could mislead voters or spread false information. It imposes strict rules on how AI tools can be used in campaign activities, requiring transparency and accountability to prevent manipulation.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a proposed law that requires creators of AI systems capable of changing their own code or behavior to register with a government agency and submit regular safety reports. It aims to ensure that these self‑evolving AIs are transparent, safe, and accountable to protect public interests.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is intended to prevent the creation and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that could act in harmful or unpredictable ways. It proposes regulations and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI technologies are designed, monitored, and used responsibly to protect public safety and security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on constructing new data centers specifically for AI to address environmental, energy, and safety concerns. It aims to regulate AI infrastructure growth, encourage sustainable practices, and prevent unchecked expansion of high‑energy‑consuming facilities.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to monitor, investigate, and regulate risks at the intersection of artificial intelligence and cyber threats. It aims to enhance national security by overseeing AI deployments in critical infrastructure, ensuring compliance, and addressing potential vulnerabilities.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” is aimed at guiding the development and deployment of artificial‑intelligence technologies so that they directly benefit American citizens, focusing on job creation, consumer protection, and ensuring the technology serves the public interest. The legislation proposes regulatory frameworks and incentives to promote responsible AI use while safeguarding privacy and encouraging innovation.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act mandates that AI developers and operators in China compile and submit reports detailing their AI system’s energy usage, performance metrics, and environmental impact. This law aims to improve transparency, promote energy efficiency, and help regulators monitor the growing AI sector’s resource consumption.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits artificial intelligence from performing any functions that are traditionally carried out by licensed medical doctors. It requires that all medical diagnoses, treatments, and patient interactions be conducted by qualified human physicians and that AI tools can only support, not replace, medical professionals.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy creates a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President. It is designed to identify and manage risks from AI and other emerging technologies and to coordinate national responses to these challenges.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to study the technology’s impacts and advise on policy. It outlines the committee’s membership, jurisdiction, and responsibilities for guiding responsible AI development and regulation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 aims to establish a framework for assessing and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It mandates regular risk evaluations, reporting requirements, and potentially imposes penalties for non-compliance.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a U.S. law that seeks to regulate artificial intelligence to ensure it is safe, transparent, and accountable, especially for high‑risk applications. It establishes standards for developers, requires risk assessments and public disclosure of AI systems, and creates enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law designed to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems, such as by setting limits on energy use and encouraging green computing practices. It requires companies that develop or deploy AI to report their environmental impacts and adopt measures that lower power consumption, carbon emissions, and waste.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: This act establishes a national framework to integrate AI literacy into K‑12 curricula, ensuring students learn basic concepts, tools, and ethical considerations. It also requires teacher training, sets standards, and allocates funding so schools can prepare students for an AI‑driven future.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a law that sets standards and guidelines to make sure that AI research is trustworthy and safe. It creates oversight and accountability so that new AI technologies are developed responsibly and can be relied on by society.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses AI to strengthen the cyber defense of critical infrastructure. The program is intended to test, develop, and evaluate AI technologies that can detect, respond to, and mitigate cyber threats to essential national infrastructure while addressing broader security and regulatory concerns.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to embed AI education into all grade levels, setting clear curriculum standards that teach students the basics of artificial intelligence, its benefits, and its risks. It also establishes guidelines for teachers’ professional development, equitable access to AI tools, and safeguards to protect student privacy and promote responsible AI use.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes rules to ensure that artificial‑intelligence systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs when processing claims are transparent, fair, and properly monitored. It requires the VA to audit AI decisions, provide clear explanations to veterans, and enforce accountability for any biases or errors that could affect claim outcomes.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a law that requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to be clear about when and how it uses artificial‑intelligence tools in its services. It mandates that the VA publicly share information on the AI systems it deploys, their purposes, and any potential impacts so veterans and the public can understand and hold the VA accountable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a nationwide campaign to raise public awareness and understanding of artificial intelligence, outlining programs that educate citizens about AI technologies and their societal impacts. It also sets up funding mechanisms and partnerships with schools and community groups to promote AI literacy across all age groups.
